theorem_statement: For Delta I = 1 M1+E2 transitions in oriented nuclei with negative delta, the linear polarization P(90) crosses zero at a remarkably small threshold |delta_crit| ~ 0.15 (corresponding to only ~2.2% E2 admixture). For all negative mixing ratios with |delta| > 0.15, the linear polarization P(90) is strictly positive (P > 0). Consequently, any M1-dominated small root with |delta| >= 0.20 (including delta = -0.26 in 187Au and delta = -0.37 in 135Pr) naturally produces positive linear polarization. A measured positive asymmetry (A > 0 or P > 0) is fundamentally non-identifying and CANNOT be used to assert E2 dominance or select the large root |delta| > 1.
resolution_requirement: To uniquely resolve the mixing ratio ambiguity, experiments must either achieve linear polarization precision sigma_P <= 0.05 - 0.08 (sufficient for >3-sigma separation of small vs large root polarization amplitudes), or measure the internal conversion coefficient alpha_K, which is strictly quadratic in delta^2 without interference terms.
